{
  "summary": "Adds opt-in CMake registration to run Python functional tests directly through CTest when configured with -DBUILD_FUNCTIONAL_TESTS=ON (requiring CMake 4.4 or newer). It adds --dump-ctest and --ctest-direct modes to test_runner.py, models shared cache setup and teardown as CTest fixtures, and avoids directory collisions across concurrent variants with unique temporary paths. The macOS native CI job is updated to exercise this combined unit and functional CTest execution workflow.",
  "problem": "Functional tests can only be orchestrated through test_runner.py rather than standard CTest commands. This prevents developers from scheduling unit and functional tests together, filtering tests or rerunning failures through standard CTest and IDE interfaces, and reporting individual test results and timings to dashboards like CDash.",
  "evidence": [
    "PR description: 'Scheduling unit and functional tests together may improve parallel execution. It also enables per-test results and timings to be uploaded to our Bitcoin Core CDash instance, helping track failures and runtime changes across builds.'",
    "Commit 7d3bbcffaa: 'Native discovery makes functional cases available to CTest scheduling, filters and dashboards alongside unit tests.'",
    "Commit f574198736 notes real-world collisions: 'Concurrent variants of the same script can observe the same wall-clock value on macOS and select an identical temporary directory. The second test then fails before framework setup completes.'"

result.summary: Adds opt-in CMake registration to run Python functional tests directly through CTest when configured with -DBUILD_FUNCTIONAL_TESTS=ON (requiring CMake 4.4 or newer). It adds --dump-ctest and --ctest-direct modes to test_runner.py, models shared cache setup and teardown as CTest fixtures, and avoids directory collisions across concurrent variants with unique temporary paths. The macOS native CI job is updated to exercise this combined unit and functional CTest execution workflow.
result.problem: Functional tests can only be orchestrated through test_runner.py rather than standard CTest commands. This prevents developers from scheduling unit and functional tests together, filtering tests or rerunning failures through standard CTest and IDE interfaces, and reporting individual test results and timings to dashboards like CDash.
evidence: PR description: 'Scheduling unit and functional tests together may improve parallel execution. It also enables per-test results and timings to be uploaded to our Bitcoin Core CDash instance, helping track failures and runtime changes across builds.'
Commit 7d3bbcffaa: 'Native discovery makes functional cases available to CTest scheduling, filters and dashboards alongside unit tests.'

Commit f574198736 notes real-world collisions: 'Concurrent variants of the same script can observe the same wall-clock value on macOS and select an identical temporary directory. The second test then fails before framework setup completes.'
result.scope_notes: Requires CMake 4.4+ only when BUILD_FUNCTIONAL_TESTS=ON is set; builds with the option disabled keep the existing CMake minimum.
result.changed_since_previous: Dropped the fallback discovery script for older CMake versions in favor of strictly requiring CMake 4.4+ when the option is enabled; switched temporary test directory generation to UUID suffixes to prevent collision races during concurrent execution; and set allow_abbrev=False on the test runner argument parser.
result.card: Adds opt-in CMake integration to register Python functional tests as individual CTest targets alongside unit tests when built with CMake 4.4 or newer. Functional tests previously required orchestration through test_runner.py, preventing developers from using standard CTest flags or IDE runners and blocking per-test reporting to dashboards like CDash. The change introduces test manifest emission and single-test execution modes in the runner, manages the shared test cache via CTest fixtures, and enables the workflow in the macOS native CI job. The existing test runner remains the default for standard local builds.

risk.why: Mistakes are confined to test harness execution and the native macOS CI job, with no impact on production node binaries or consensus logic.
